a288cd23f0.q: What happened to multifamily property values when the Federal Reserve raised interest rates 550 basis points between 2022 and 2023?
a288cd23f0.a: Multifamily values started to compress or cap rates started to expand. From 2022 onward, anyone who bought in 2021 saw those properties suffer. Values dropped 20 to 30 percent on multifamily across the country. This occurred because when debt becomes more expensive, buyers can only afford lower-priced properties, forcing values downward to accommodate higher interest rates.

53a1d53034.q: Why did multifamily investors use floating rate debt during the low interest rate period instead of locking in fixed rates?
53a1d53034.a: Investors used floating rate debt because it offered even cheaper terms initially than fixed rates at 3 or 4 percent. They wanted to outbid competitors on property prices and felt they could compete better with floating rates, even though they were excited and wanted to play in the market. This strategy backfired when rates rose dramatically.

acb96fb47d.q: How many apartment units is Kansas City behind on development since the 2008 crash?
acb96fb47d.a: Kansas City is 18,000 apartment units behind on development from 2008 to now. This shortage occurred because after the 2008 crisis, people were unwilling and unable to borrow money to build new multifamily properties, creating a long-term supply constraint that compounded over the next decade.

91cc0fa8c4.q: What percentage of new apartment deliveries during the boom cycle were concentrated in Sunbelt markets?

This concentration occurred because investors followed the narrative that these markets had the highest growth and lowest cap rates, exacerbating the overbuild problem.
